payload.title: Automated evaluation harness for translation quality
payload.description:
As the owner of a multilingual publication, I want to know automatically whether polishing helps and whether a rule is trustworthy, so nothing ships on a guess even though nobody in-house reads Chinese.

Design: sections 1.5 and 3.10, rewritten for Ryan's decision of 2026-11-13: NO paid human translators and NO native-reader panel. Every panel-based measure is replaced by automated evaluation only:
- a development set and a held-out set of published Stories (held-out never used for tuning, re-drawn when packs change materially);
- a per-language regression suite in CI, no model: every detector's must-fire and must-not-fire examples, every parity rule with real past failures, segmentation cases (Spanish and Chinese built together);
- bilingual model judges (span-level, quoting both sides, repeated passes must agree);
- source-versus-target parity checks (numbers, names, links, structure, quotations);
- distance from a measured native baseline on the pack's features (pronouns, conjunctions, 的, 被, clause length), raw against polished;
- back-translation is a reading aid only, never a gate and never a score.
State plainly in every report this story produces that nobody in-house can verify Chinese quality, so all of these measures are proxies, not proof of how native readers would judge the pages. After launch, volunteer correctors' edits are a free continuing signal, never a requirement.

A rule drives rewrites only at about 9 in 10 correct on held-out examples, measured per language, as a starting bar (Ryan 2026-11-13). Stock phrasing the evaluation finds is reported to the English Story.

```gherkin
Feature: We know, by automatic measures, whether polishing helps
  Scenario: Polished and raw translations are compared on held-out Stories
    Given thirty held-out Stories translated raw and polished
    When the bilingual judges and parity checks score both versions
    Then the report gives faithfulness errors per 1,000 characters for each
    And gives typography and translationese findings per 1,000 characters for each
    And gives the distance from the native baseline for each
    And says plainly that nobody in-house can verify Chinese quality and these measures are proxies

  Scenario: A rule earns the right to rewrite
    Given held-out examples labelled by the bilingual judges and the parity rules
    When a rule's hits are compared with the labels
    Then the rule's precision is stored on the policy for that language
    And a rule below about nine in ten only advises

  Scenario: The regression suite guards every language in CI
    Given the Spanish and Chinese regression suites
    When CI runs
    Then every detector, parity rule and segmentation case passes with no model call

  Scenario: Back-translation is shown but never decides
    Given a translated Story and an English back-translation made by a different model
    When the evaluation report is built
    Then the back-translation appears as a reading aid
    And no pass or fail depends on it

  Scenario: Polishing that makes faithfulness worse is a defect
    Given the held-out results show more faithfulness errors after polishing
    Then the report marks the polish loop as failing for that language
    And that language publishes raw translation plus parity checks until it is fixed
```
